skill.name: amazon-listing-competitor-analysis-skill
skill.description: Analyze a competitor Amazon listing by ASIN with BrowserAct extraction and a structured competitive analysis framework.
skill.summary: Turns Amazon ASIN research into competitor strengths, market gaps, and opportunity points.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill performs expected BrowserAct network operations and runs a bundled Python script. Credential handling is the main concern because instructions encourage users to provide an API key to the agent. No prompt injection attempt or hidden malicious code was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: API key may be disclosed through chat instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide the key to the agent. Require users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY locally and never paste the key into chat.

remediation.issue: Marketplace URL is accepted without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate marketplace_url against known Amazon marketplace domains before sending it to BrowserAct.

remediation.issue: Third-party network use is central to the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Document that ASIN, marketplace URL, task metadata, and API authorization are sent to BrowserAct during extraction.

content.value_statement: Amazon teams need reliable competitor signals before changing content, offers, or launch plans. This skill extracts listing data by ASIN and turns it into grounded market opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Runs a BrowserAct workflow for one ASIN and marketplace URL through the bundled Python script.
Retrieves listing fields such as title, price, rating, images, seller details, bullets, details, and reviews.
Polls BrowserAct task status and reports progress until completion, failure, or timeout.
Guides analysis of content strategy, keyword placement, visuals, buyer reviews, and market gaps.
Produces strategic opportunity points for the user's brand based on extracted listing evidence.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct API key, Python, internet access, and a reachable Amazon listing.
Depends on BrowserAct workflow availability and the data visible on the Amazon page.
Analyzes one ASIN per script run and does not compare multiple products automatically.
Does not verify sales, conversion rate, advertising data, or private Seller Central metrics.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Competitor Listing Teardown
use_cases.description: Review a single ASIN to understand copy structure, visible proof points, and buyer response before revising your market plan.

use_cases.title: Find Launch Positioning Gaps
use_cases.description: Use competitor listing evidence to identify under-served buyer needs, missing proof, and defensible product angles.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Amazon SEO Signals
use_cases.description: Map how a competitor places primary, secondary, and long-tail terms across title, bullets, description, and A plus content.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One ASIN
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze Amazon ASIN [ASIN] on [marketplace URL]. Summarize competitor strengths, market gaps, and opportunities for my product.

prompt_templates.title: Review Keyword Placement
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this ASIN [ASIN] to map keyword placement across title, bullets, description, and A plus content. Highlight weak search intents.

prompt_templates.title: Mine Buyer Needs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze ASIN [ASIN] and focus on buyer reviews. Separate praised benefits, recurring complaints, unmet needs, and offer opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Strategic Opportunity Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze ASIN [ASIN] for my planned product in [category]. Compare content, visuals, proof, reviews, and gaps into prioritized opportunities.

output_examples.input: Analyze one competitor ASIN for a pre-launch kitchen product.
output: Competitor strengths: clear title formula, review-backed durability claims, and image proof for common use cases.
Market gaps: weak care instructions, limited size comparison, and repeated review questions about compatibility.
Opportunity points: own compatibility clarity, add proof-led images, and address maintenance concerns early.

output_examples.input: Review keyword placement for an Amazon home product listing.
output: Primary terms appear early in the title and first two bullets.
Long-tail terms are thin in the description and buyer language is missing from image captions.
Search opportunity: emphasize use-case terms that reviewers mention but the competitor underuses.

output_examples.input: Find buyer needs from competitor reviews.
output: Positive reviews validate ease of setup and compact storage.
Mixed reviews mention confusing sizing and unclear installation expectations.
Product opportunity: package clearer sizing guidance and support materials as trust builders.

best_practices: Set the BrowserAct API key as an environment variable before running the skill.
Use the correct regional Amazon marketplace URL for the ASIN under review.
Base every strategic point on extracted listing fields or review evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users to paste API keys into chat or shared documents.
Do not treat one competitor listing as a full market study.
Do not invent unavailable metrics such as conversion rate, sales, or ad spend.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs an Amazon ASIN and optionally a regional Amazon marketplace URL.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses BrowserAct and expects the BrowserAct API key in an environment variable.

faq.question: Can it analyze multiple competitors at once?
faq.answer: No. The bundled script handles one ASIN per run.

faq.question: What does the final analysis include?
faq.answer: It covers competitor strengths, keyword placement, visual strategy, buyer feedback, market gaps, and opportunity points.

faq.question: Can it access private Amazon seller data?
faq.answer: No. It works from visible listing data returned by the BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
